name: 尤利西斯·辛普森·格兰特

points.place: 俄亥俄州波因特普莱森特
points.title: 早年生活
points.description: 格兰特于1822年4月27日出生在俄亥俄州波因特普莱森特的一个制革匠家庭。他的原名是海勒姆·尤利西斯·格兰特，后来名字被误记为尤利西斯·辛普森·格兰特。童年时期，他展现出对马匹的天赋和对军事的浓厚兴趣。1839年，他通过国会推荐进入西点军校，开启了他的军事生涯。这段早期生活培养了他坚韧不拔的性格和对细节的关注，这些品质后来成为他军事成功的关键因素。
points.descriptionEn: Grant was born on April 27, 1822, in Point Pleasant, Ohio, to a tanner family. His original name was Hiram Ulysses Grant, but it was mistakenly recorded as Ulysses S. Grant. During his childhood, he displayed a natural talent with horses and a keen interest in military affairs. In 1839, he was appointed to the United States Military Academy at West Point through a congressional nomination, beginning his military career. This early life cultivated his perseverance and attention to detail, qualities that later became crucial to his military success.

points.title: 军旅生涯初期
points.description: 从西点军校毕业后，格兰特被派往各地军事驻地服役，参与了美墨战争。在战争中，他表现出色，特别是在莫尔洛斯战役和韦拉克鲁斯战役中展现了卓越的军事才能。战后，他被派往西海岸，因思念家人而酗酒问题加剧，最终于1854年辞职。这段经历虽然以辞职告终，但他在战争中获得的实战经验和对军事战略的深刻理解，为他后来在内战中的成功奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After graduating from West Point, Grant was assigned to various military posts and participated in the Mexican-American War. He distinguished himself, particularly in the battles of Molino del Rey and Veracruz, showcasing exceptional military abilities. Post-war, he was stationed on the West Coast where his drinking problems worsened due to homesickness, leading to his resignation in 1854. Although this period ended with his resignation, the practical experience and strategic insights gained during the war laid the foundation for his later success in the Civil War.

points.place: 伊利诺伊州和西部战场
points.title: 内战崛起
points.description: 美国内战爆发后，格兰特重新加入军队，被任命为伊利诺伊州志愿军团上校。他迅速展现出卓越的军事才能，先后指挥多场关键战役，包括亨利堡和多纳尔森堡战役，赢得'无条件投降'格兰特的绰号。1862年，他在夏洛战役中击败南方军队，巩固了联邦在西部的控制权。1863年，他指挥维克斯堡战役，通过一系列精心策划的行动，成功夺取了密西西比河上的这一战略要地，将南方邦联一分为二，成为内战的转折点之一。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of the American Civil War, Grant re-entered military service and was appointed colonel of the 21st Illinois Volunteer Infantry. He quickly demonstrated exceptional military talent, commanding several key battles including the captures of Fort Henry and Fort Donelson, earning the nickname 'Unconditional Surrender Grant.' In 1862, he defeated Confederate forces at the Battle of Shiloh, consolidating Union control in the West. In 1863, he led the Vicksburg Campaign, through a series of meticulously planned operations, successfully capturing this strategic stronghold on the Mississippi River, effectively splitting the Confederacy in two and marking a turning point in the war.

points.place: 弗吉尼亚州和华盛顿特区
points.title: 总司令与胜利
points.description: 1864年，林肯任命格兰特为联邦军总司令，并授予中将军衔。格兰特采取'全面战争'策略，与罗伯特·李率领的南方军队展开消耗战。他指挥了荒野战役、斯波特瑟尔法尼亚战役和冷港战役等血腥战斗，虽然伤亡惨重，但最终迫使李将军投降。1865年4月9日，格兰特在弗吉尼亚州的阿波马托克斯法院接受了李将军的投降，标志着美国内战的结束。作为胜利者，格兰特展现了宽容和和解的精神，允许南方军队保留武器和荣誉，为战后重建奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1864, Lincoln appointed Grant as General-in-Chief of the Union Army and granted him the rank of lieutenant general. Grant adopted a 'total war' strategy, engaging in a war of attrition against Robert E. Lee's Confederate forces. He commanded bloody battles including the Wilderness Campaign, Spotsylvania Court House, and Cold Harbor, suffering heavy casualties but eventually forcing Lee's surrender. On April 9, 1865, Grant accepted Lee's surrender at Appomattox Court House in Virginia, effectively ending the Civil War. As the victor, Grant demonstrated magnanimity and reconciliation, allowing Confederate soldiers to keep their weapons and honor, laying the groundwork for post-war Reconstruction.

points.title: 总统任期
points.description: 1868年，格兰特作为共和党候选人当选美国第18任总统。他的两届任期（1869-1877）见证了战后重建的关键时期。他支持《宪法》第十五修正案的通过，保障非裔美国人的投票权；推行强硬的南方重建政策，保护前奴隶的权利；签署《印度和平政策》，试图改善与原住民的关系。然而，他的政府也面临严重腐败问题，包括多名内阁成员被指控受贿。尽管如此，格兰特在推动民权、保护少数族裔权益方面的努力，为后来的民权运动奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1868, Grant was elected as the 18th President of the United States as a Republican candidate. His two terms (1869-1877) witnessed a critical period of post-war Reconstruction. He supported the passage of the 15th Amendment to the Constitution, guaranteeing voting rights for African American men; implemented a strong Reconstruction policy in the South to protect the rights of former slaves; and signed the Indian Peace Policy, attempting to improve relations with Native Americans. However, his administration also faced serious corruption issues, with several cabinet members accused of bribery. Despite these challenges, Grant's efforts in promoting civil rights and protecting minority rights laid the groundwork for later civil rights movements.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 离开白宫后，格兰特进行了全球旅行，成为国际名人。晚年，他面临严重的财务困境，投资失败导致破产。为了养活家人，他开始撰写回忆录，在生命最后几个月完成了这部作品。1885年7月23日，格兰特因喉癌去世，享年63岁。他的回忆录在他去世后出版，成为美国文学经典，也为家人提供了财务保障。作为军事英雄和总统，格兰特的遗产复杂而深远：他被视为内战胜利的关键人物，但他的总统任期也因腐败问题而受到批评。然而，他对国家统一的坚持和对民权的支持，使他成为美国历史上最具影响力的领导人之一。
points.descriptionEn: After leaving the White House, Grant embarked on a global tour, becoming an international celebrity. In his later years, he faced severe financial difficulties, losing his fortune through failed investments. To provide for his family, he began writing his memoirs, completing them in the final months of his life. On July 23, 1885, Grant died of throat cancer at the age of 63. His memoirs were published posthumously, becoming an American literary classic and providing financial security for his family. As a military hero and president, Grant's legacy is complex and profound: he is remembered as a key figure in winning the Civil War, but his presidency is also criticized for corruption issues. Nevertheless, his commitment to national unity and support for civil rights establish him as one of the most influential figures in American history.

supporter.zh: 格兰特被视为美国历史上最伟大的军事统帅之一，他以坚定的意志和卓越的军事才能赢得了内战，维护了国家统一。作为总统，他积极推动重建时期民权立法，保障非裔美国人的基本权利。他的'无条件投降'策略虽然造成巨大伤亡，但有效缩短了战争，挽救了更多生命。格兰特展现了军人的荣誉感和对国家的忠诚，他的领导风格直接、果断，体现了美国精神中的坚韧与决心。
supporter.en: Grant is regarded as one of the greatest military commanders in American history, whose unwavering will and exceptional military talent won the Civil War and preserved national unity. As president, he actively promoted civil rights legislation during Reconstruction, protecting the fundamental rights of African Americans. His 'unconditional surrender' strategy, though causing heavy casualties, effectively shortened the war and saved more lives. Grant demonstrated military honor and loyalty to the country, with a direct and decisive leadership style that embodies the resilience and determination of the American spirit.

critic.zh: 批评者认为格兰特的军事策略过于简单粗暴，导致内战中联邦军队伤亡惨重。他的总统任期被腐败问题困扰，多名内阁成员被指控受贿，政府效率低下。在印第安人政策上，他虽然试图推行和平政策，但未能阻止西部的暴力冲突。此外，格兰特对南方重建的强硬政策也引发了长期的政治分歧。批评者指出，他的领导风格缺乏灵活性，有时显得固执己见，未能有效应对战后复杂的社会经济挑战。
critic.en: Critics argue that Grant's military strategies were overly simplistic and brutal, leading to massive casualties for Union forces during the Civil War. His presidency was plagued by corruption scandals, with several cabinet members accused of bribery and government inefficiency. Regarding Indian policy, although he attempted to implement peaceful policies, he failed to prevent violent conflicts in the West. Additionally, his harsh Reconstruction policies in the South created long-term political divisions. Critics point out that his leadership style lacked flexibility, sometimes appearing stubborn and failing to effectively address the complex socioeconomic challenges of the post-war era.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，格兰特被视为一个复杂而矛盾的历史人物。他既是内战的胜利者，也是备受争议的总统。历史学家普遍承认他在军事上的卓越成就，但也批评其总统任期的腐败问题。流行文化中，格兰特的形象经历了从英雄到有缺陷的人物的转变。他的回忆录被公认为美国文学经典，展现了他作为作家的才能。近年来，随着对重建时期研究的深入，学者们重新评估了格兰特在推动民权方面的贡献，认为他的历史遗产比传统认知更为复杂和正面。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Grant is viewed as a complex and contradictory historical figure. He is simultaneously recognized as the victor of the Civil War and a controversial president. Historians generally acknowledge his exceptional military achievements but criticize the corruption issues during his presidency. In popular culture, Grant's image has evolved from hero to flawed individual. His memoirs are widely regarded as an American literary classic, showcasing his talent as a writer. In recent years, with deeper research into the Reconstruction era, scholars have reassessed Grant's contributions to civil rights, arguing that his historical legacy is more complex and positive than traditionally perceived.

self.zh: 只要战争还在继续，我就不会停止战斗。
self.en: I propose to fight it out on this line if it takes all summer.

others.zh: 格兰特将军是战争中最了不起的人。他沉默寡言，行动迅速，一旦下定决心，就坚定不移。
others.en: General Grant is the greatest man of the age. He is silent and quick, and once he makes up his mind, nothing can turn him from his purpose.
